title: 2007 HMMT February Calculus Problem 4
statement: Find the real number \(\alpha\) such that the curve \(f(x)=e^{x}\) is tangent to the curve \(g(x)=\alpha x^{2}\).

solutions.text: \(\mathbf{e}^{\mathbf{2} / 4}\). Suppose tangency occurs at \(x=x_{0}\). Then \(e^{x_{0}}=\alpha x_{0}^{2}\) and \(f^{\prime}\left(x_{0}\right)=2 \alpha x_{0}\). On the other hand, \(f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\), so \(\alpha x_{0}^{2}=2 \alpha x_{0}\). Clearly, \(\alpha=0\) and \(x_{0}=0\) are impossible, so it must be that \(x_{0}=2\). Then \(\alpha=e^{x_{0}} /\left(x_{0}^{2}\right)=e^{2} / 4\).
